# Notes on the Topology of Symplectic Quotients

## Introduction and Motivation

These notes accompany a lecture devoted to the topology of symplectic quotients, and more generally to quotients arising in related geometric categories. Our principal aim is twofold. First, we wish to advertise a simple point: many computations that appear formidable in the algebraic or complex-analytic category become remarkably tractable once one passes to the symplectic setting. The symplectic category furnishes tools—moment maps, equivariant cohomology, local normal forms—that streamline calculations which might otherwise require heavy machinery. Second, we wish to put this philosophy into practice by presenting new computations for a family of spaces of particular interest: weighted projective spaces. These spaces, though elementary to define, carry a rich orbifold structure whose cohomological invariants are worth understanding in detail, and they serve as an excellent testing ground for the techniques we develop.

## Orbifolds in the Symplectic Category

We begin with a brief but self-contained exposition of how orbifold structures naturally arise when one performs symplectic reduction. When a compact Lie group (or more generally a torus) acts on a symplectic manifold in a Hamiltonian fashion, the reduced space obtained at a given level of the moment map need not be smooth: points with nontrivial stabilizer under the group action descend to orbifold singularities in the quotient. We recall the basic local model for this phenomenon, emphasizing how the isotropy data of the original action is encoded in the orbifold charts of the reduced space.

Having established this local picture, we turn to a discussion of the techniques available for understanding the global topology of such quotients. Central among these are the methods of equivariant cohomology and the Kirwan map, which relates the equivariant cohomology of the original manifold to the ordinary (or orbifold) cohomology of the reduction. We review the relevant surjectivity and kernel-description results, since these form the backbone of the computations to follow. Along the way we highlight how the combinatorics of the moment map image—and in particular the isotropy weights along its faces—control the orbifold structure of the quotient without our needing to invoke any auxiliary combinatorial gadget.

## Chen–Ruan Cohomology of Abelian Symplectic Reductions

The topological groundwork laid in the first part of the notes is then put to use in computing the Chen–Ruan orbifold cohomology ring of symplectic reductions by abelian groups. The Chen–Ruan cohomology ring refines the ordinary cohomology of an orbifold by incorporating contributions from its twisted sectors, and its ring structure—governed by the orbifold cup product—is sensitive to delicate geometric data associated to the singularities.

We show how the equivariant techniques described above extend naturally to this orbifold setting: the twisted sectors of an abelian symplectic quotient can be identified with reductions of certain fixed-point loci in the original manifold, and the Kirwan-type surjectivity results generalize to give a presentation of the full Chen–Ruan ring. This yields an explicit and computable description of the orbifold cohomology ring purely in terms of equivariant data on the original Hamiltonian space, again without recourse to stack-theoretic language.

## Application to Weighted Projective Spaces

The notes conclude by specializing this general theory to the case of weighted projective spaces, which arise as abelian symplectic reductions of complex vector spaces by the circle. For these spaces several natural cohomological rings can be considered: the ordinary cohomology ring, the Chen–Ruan orbifold cohomology ring, and, when available, rings arising from the toric or algebraic perspective. A substantial portion of the concluding discussion is devoted to comparing these various rings directly, exhibiting explicit generators and relations in each case and clarifying how they relate to one another.

## Methodological Remark

Throughout the notes, we adopt a deliberately hands-on approach: all computations are carried out directly, using only the symplectic and equivariant cohomological framework described above. In particular, we consciously avoid any appeal to the language of stacky fans or labeled moment polytopes, which are common tools in the toric and stack-theoretic literature for encoding the combinatorial data of weighted projective spaces and related quotients. Our purpose in doing so is to demonstrate that the symplectic techniques alone suffice to recover—and indeed to organize quite transparently—all the cohomological information one might want, without requiring the reader to first absorb a parallel combinatorial formalism.

# Symplectic Techniques for Computing Orbifold Cohomology of Symplectic Quotients

## Introduction and Motivation

These notes are devoted to exploring the topology of symplectic quotients through the lens of computational techniques native to the symplectic category itself, rather than relying on the algebraic or combinatorial machinery that has become standard in the toric and orbifold literature. Our central aim is to demonstrate that many of the deep results concerning the cohomological structure of symplectic reductions—particularly the Chen-Ruan orbifold cohomology ring—can be derived using tools that are intrinsic to symplectic geometry: moment maps, equivariant cohomology, symplectic reduction, and the geometry of group actions on symplectic manifolds.

The primary case studies we consider are **abelian symplectic reductions**, with special emphasis on **weighted projective spaces**, which arise as symplectic quotients of $\mathbb{C}^n$ by the action of a torus (or more generally, a product of a torus and cyclic groups) with appropriately chosen weights. Weighted projective spaces serve as an excellent testing ground for these techniques: they are simple enough to admit fully explicit computations, yet rich enough to exhibit genuinely orbifold phenomena, including nontrivial isotropy groups, twisted sectors, and subtle ring structures in their Chen-Ruan cohomology.

## Departing from the Stacky and Combinatorial Approach

In the existing literature, computations of orbifold cohomology for spaces such as weighted projective spaces are most commonly carried out using the formalism of **stacky fans** (in the sense of Borisov-Chen-Smith) or through **labeled moment polytopes**, which encode the combinatorial data of the toric orbifold structure. These approaches, while powerful and conceptually elegant, require the reader to first translate the symplectic or complex-analytic picture into a combinatorial one, and then to perform the orbifold cohomology computation within that combinatorial framework. This translation, though standard for experts in toric geometry, can obscure the underlying symplectic geometry and imposes a nontrivial barrier to entry for readers whose primary background is in symplectic topology rather than algebraic or toric geometry.

The approach taken in these notes deliberately avoids this detour. Instead, we work directly with the symplectic quotient construction: starting from a Hamiltonian torus action on a symplectic vector space (or more general symplectic manifold), we perform symplectic reduction at a regular value of the moment map, and analyze the resulting orbifold using tools such as:

- the inertia orbifold and its symplectic/geometric description as a disjoint union of quotients of fixed-point sets,
- equivariant cohomology of the group action before reduction, via the Cartan model or Kirwan's surjectivity techniques,
- the Kirwan map and its kernel, which allow one to pass from equivariant cohomology of the ambient space to the cohomology of the reduced space,
- explicit identification of twisted sectors and their degree shifting numbers directly from the symplectic normal bundle data at fixed loci.

This symplectic-theoretic route allows one to bypass the need for stacky fans entirely: the data of isotropy groups, age gradings, and the ring structure on the orbifold cohomology can all be extracted from the moment map picture and the linear algebra of the torus action on the ambient symplectic vector space.

## Structure and Content of the Computations

We begin with a review of the necessary background: the definition of symplectic reduction, the structure of orbifolds as quotients of manifolds by locally free group actions, and the construction of the Chen-Ruan orbifold cohomology ring, including the twisted sector decomposition and the orbifold cup product defined via obstruction bundles and moduli of orbifold stable maps of genus zero with appropriate ramification.

We then specialize to the case of **abelian quotients**, where the moment map picture is particularly transparent: the reduced space is obtained as
$$
X_{\text{red}} = \mu^{-1}(0)/T
$$
for a Hamiltonian torus $T$ acting on a symplectic vector space $V$ (or more general symplectic manifold), and the fixed loci of the induced inertia orbifold correspond to sub-tori of isotropy and their associated weight spaces. We show how to compute:

- the additive structure of $H^*_{CR}(X_{\text{red}})$ as a direct sum over twisted sectors,
- the age (degree shifting number) of each sector directly from the weights of the torus action on the normal bundle,
- the ring structure, including the orbifold product between untwisted and twisted classes, using explicit equivariant cohomology classes and their images under the Kirwan map.

Specializing further, we carry out the complete computation for **weighted projective spaces** $\mathbb{P}(a_0, \ldots, a_n)$, recovering their Chen-Ruan cohomology ring explicitly in terms of generators and relations, and identifying the twisted sectors with the various "singular strata" corresponding to common divisors among the weights $a_i$.

## New Comparisons and Contributions

Beyond re-deriving known results by new means, these notes offer several **new computations and comparisons** among the various cohomological invariants associated with weighted projective spaces. In particular, we compare:

- the **Chen-Ruan orbifold cohomology ring**, computed via the symplectic/equivariant approach outlined above,
- the **Chen-Ruan cohomology ring as computed via stacky fans**, in order to cross-check consistency and illuminate the dictionary between the two languages,
- the **ordinary singular cohomology ring** of the underlying topological space (the coarse moduli space) of the weighted projective space, which typically differs substantially from the orbifold cohomology ring due to the contribution of twisted sectors,
- and, where relevant, the **Chen-Ruan cohomology as it relates to the crepant resolution conjecture**, comparing the orbifold cohomology ring of $\mathbb{P}(a_0,\ldots,a_n)$ with the cohomology ring of an appropriate crepant resolution, when one exists.

These comparisons serve both as consistency checks on the symplectic method and as a means of highlighting subtle points—such as the appearance of fractional grading, the non-commutativity or non-associativity pitfalls that must be avoided in defining the orbifold product, and the sensitivity of the ring structure to the precise combinatorics of the weights $a_i$.

## Pedagogical Aim

A guiding theme throughout these notes is the **relative ease and accessibility** of the symplectic approach for readers whose background lies in symplectic and differential geometry rather than algebraic geometry or the theory of stacks. By keeping the discussion grounded in moment maps, equivariant cohomology, and explicit linear algebra of torus weights, we hope to make the subject of orbifold cohomology—and in particular the rich example of weighted projective spaces—accessible to a broader audience, and to illustrate that many computations traditionally viewed as requiring heavy algebro-geometric machinery can in fact be carried out, often more transparently, using only the symplectic category's native toolkit. It is our hope that this exposition will serve both as a self-contained introduction to Chen-Ruan orbifold cohomology for symplectic geometers, and as a resource for further computations in the broader landscape of symplectic and Hamiltonian orbifold quotients.

# Chen-Ruan Cohomology of Abelian Symplectic Reductions

**Abstract**

Symplectic reduction is a fundamental tool for constructing new symplectic and Kähler spaces from group actions—toric varieties being the prototypical example when the group is abelian. When the action is not free, the quotient acquires orbifold singularities, and the ordinary cohomology of the quotient often fails to capture the full geometric picture. Chen-Ruan cohomology provides the correct orbifold-theoretic replacement: as a vector space it is built from the cohomology of the inertia orbifold (contributions from fixed-point loci of group elements), and it comes equipped with a quantum-corrected ring structure arising from orbifold Gromov-Witten theory.

In this talk, we describe an explicit, combinatorial approach to computing the Chen-Ruan cohomology of symplectic orbifold reductions by compact abelian groups—generalizing the familiar Batyrev-style description of the cohomology of toric varieties in terms of the combinatorics of a moment polytope or fan. Rather than invoking stack-theoretic machinery, we work directly with the moment map picture: fixed loci of the inertia orbifold are identified with strata of the polytope, and the additive structure of Chen-Ruan cohomology is assembled from the ordinary cohomology of these strata, twisted by degree shifts coming from the local isotropy representations.

We will illustrate the method with weighted projective spaces and other simple abelian quotients, showing how the extra "twisted sector" classes account for the discrepancy between ordinary and orbifold cohomology, and we discuss how this combinatorial model interacts with the ring structure and the associated quantum corrections predicted by mirror symmetry.

# Cohomology Rings of Weighted Projective Spaces via Symplectic Reduction

Weighted projective space $\mathbb{P}(w_0, w_1, \ldots, w_n)$ arises as the symplectic quotient $S^{2n+1}/\!/_w U(1)$, where $U(1)$ acts with weights $w_0, \ldots, w_n$ on $\mathbb{C}^{n+1} \supset S^{2n+1}$, making it a natural setting for applying the Kirwan/Duistermaat-Heckman machinery of symplectic reduction. Via the Kirwan map, the equivariant cohomology $H^*_{U(1)}(S^{2n+1})$ surjects onto $H^*(\mathbb{P}(w_0,\ldots,w_n))$, with the equivariant cohomology of the ambient space computed as $H^*_{U(1)}(\mathbb{C}^{n+1}) \cong \mathbb{Q}[u]$, so that the weighted projective space inherits its ring structure as a quotient by the ideal generated by the equivariant Euler class relation $\prod_i (w_i u) = 0$ restricted appropriately, or more precisely as $\mathbb{Q}[x]/(x^{n+1})$ in rational cohomology—**identical to ordinary $\mathbb{CP}^n$** despite the differing weights, since rational cohomology cannot detect the orbifold structure encoded in the weights. The distinction between different weight systems only becomes visible integrally or through the Chen-Ruan orbifold cohomology, where twisted sectors indexed by isotropy data (age gradings from the weights $w_i$) contribute additional classes, or via equivariant methods that retain the weight-dependent relations before passing to the quotient, illustrating how symplectic reduction provides a unified framework in which the "coarse" rational answer is universal, while finer invariants require tracking the residual torsion and stacky structure inherited from the weighted $U(1)$-action.

# Abstract

Orbifold cohomology, introduced by Chen–Ruan in the context of orbifold Gromov–Witten theory, provides a refined cohomological invariant for orbifolds that incorporates contributions from twisted sectors associated to isotropy group elements. While the original definition relies on algebro-geometric or complex-analytic constructions of the inertia stack, computing orbifold cohomology explicitly for singular quotient spaces can be technically demanding. In this work, we demonstrate how symplectic techniques—particularly the machinery of symplectic reduction, moment maps, and equivariant cohomology—offer a streamlined and geometrically transparent approach to these computations.

Our method exploits the presentation of orbifolds as symplectic quotients $M /\!\!/ G$ arising from Hamiltonian group actions, allowing the twisted sectors of the inertia orbifold to be organized via the combinatorics of isotropy data encoded in the moment map fibers. By passing to the Cartan model for equivariant cohomology and analyzing the fixed-point loci of the residual torus action on the reduced space, we obtain an additive decomposition of orbifold cohomology as a direct sum over conjugacy classes of isotropy groups, each contributing a shifted copy of the cohomology of the corresponding fixed locus. This reformulation reduces the problem to computations in ordinary equivariant cohomology, circumventing the need for explicit stack-theoretic or resolution-based arguments, and naturally accommodates the age (fermionic shifting) grading via localization data at fixed points.

We illustrate the power of this approach through the family of weighted projective spaces $\mathbb{P}(w_0, \ldots, w_n)$, realized as symplectic reductions of $\mathbb{C}^{n+1}$ by a Hamiltonian $S^1$-action with weights $w_i$. Using our symplectic framework, we compute the Chen–Ruan orbifold cohomology ring $H^*_{CR}(\mathbb{P}(w_0,\ldots,w_n))$ explicitly in terms of twisted sector contributions indexed by age-shifted classes supported on coordinate subspaces fixed by cyclic isotropy. We then compare this ring with the Chen–Ruan cohomology obtained via crepant resolutions, and with the closely related Batyrev–Cox “fan cohomology” and stringy Chow ring construed from the toric data of the weighted projective space. While all three constructions agree additively—reflecting the McKay correspondence for abelian quotient singularities—we show that the ring structures can differ in subtle ways tied to the choice of orbifold versus resolved geometry, particularly in the appearance of relations governed by the extremal rays of the resolved fan versus the symplectic cut loci in our construction. This comparison clarifies the precise sense in which orbifold cohomology, quantum corrected products, and toric stringy invariants coincide for weighted projective spaces, and highlights the computational advantages of the symplectic perspective for more general orbifold quotients.

# Symplectic Quotients, Orbifolds, and the Chen-Ruan Cohomology of Weighted Projective Spaces

Weighted projective spaces provide one of the most instructive families of examples through which to study the interplay between symplectic reduction, orbifold geometry, and stringy invariants. Given a tuple of positive integers $(w_0, w_1, \dots, w_n)$, the weighted projective space $\mathbb{P}(w_0, \dots, w_n)$ arises as the symplectic (Marsden–Weinstein–Meyer) quotient of $\mathbb{C}^{n+1} \setminus \{0\}$ by the diagonal circle action $t \cdot (z_0, \dots, z_n) = (t^{w_0} z_0, \dots, t^{w_n} z_n)$, at a regular value of the associated moment map; equivalently, it is the toric variety corresponding to a simplex whose edge lattice lengths encode the weights. Unless the weights are pairwise coprime, this quotient fails to be a smooth manifold, acquiring instead isolated (or higher-dimensional) *orbifold singularities* whose local isotropy groups are cyclic groups determined by the weights. This makes $\mathbb{P}(w_0,\dots,w_n)$ a paradigmatic example of a *symplectic orbifold*: a space locally modeled on $\mathbb{R}^{2n}/\Gamma$ for finite subgroups $\Gamma \subset U(n)$, compatible with a global symplectic form descending from reduction. To capture the geometry hidden in these singularities, one passes to the *inertia orbifold*, whose components—indexed by conjugacy classes of isotropy elements—give rise to twisted sectors in addition to the untwisted sector corresponding to the underlying space. Chen–Ruan cohomology assembles the ordinary cohomology of all these sectors into a single graded vector space, with degree shifts prescribed by *age* (or degree-shifting) numbers computed from the local group actions, and equips this direct sum with a quantum-corrected, orbifold cup product incorporating contributions from orbifold Gromov–Witten invariants of degree-zero stable maps. For weighted projective spaces, the combinatorics of the weights make both the sector decomposition and the age grading fully explicit, allowing one to compute the Chen–Ruan cohomology ring by hand and to compare it directly with the Chen–Ruan cohomology of a crepant resolution, thereby furnishing a concrete testing ground for the Cohomological Crepant Resolution Conjecture and for broader themes in mirror symmetry and orbifold Gromov–Witten theory.
